title: No drummer, and a book of eight arrangements, some rejected by Basie
summary: Max Roach and Shadow Wilson are unavailable, a white drummer fills in, and the band's few charts include rejects from Basie and Dizzy's Night in Tunisia.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: And during the wartime situation, all musicians were hard to find. We were fortunate to get these people. We had hoped to have either Max Roach or Shadow Wilson with the band, but somebody had scooped both of them up. I think Max Roach was with Benny Carter at that particular time, and I don't know exactly what Shadow was doing. I know a little later he was with the Basie band. I don't know whether he was with Basie or not when the band started. But I know he wasn't available. I think he might have been in the Army.

But after trying to get drummers, we couldn't... So there was a fellow, and I don't know his name because I never really knew what his name was. He was a very nice guy. He was a White fellow. And he came to play drums with the band.

The band had... We had eight arrangements. We had a 17-piece band, eight arrangements. About four of these arrangements Count Basie had given us, and they were things that arrangers had given him that he had rejected. One of them, I remember, was "Our Delight", which Tadd Dameron wrote

for Basie, but it wasn't Basie's type of tune. And we had three ballads that we gave us that had been... I don't know who they'd been written for. The other arrangements were one arrangement by Budd Johnson called "Stay In The Mood For Love." There was another one... Dizzy had his "Night In Tunisia" and "Round Midnight." Oh, he had another blues, too. There was a blues that Dizzy wrote. It was a vocal that Billie sang. And then there was a Lucky Thompson arrangement. So there must have been nine arrangements that we had. Or else... No, there had to be... I said three ballads. Maybe there were two ballads that Basie gave us. Because I knew that we only had eight written arrangements!

So the band rehearsed on Wednesday, it rehearsed on Thursday. Our first job was Friday night in Wilmington, Delaware. I'm wondering how in the world that this band, this big band of 17 pieces, is going to play a dance with eight arrangements! Well, I had worked with bands of 13-14 pieces around Washington locally, and everything we played practically was music.
